page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dlsv6 virtual machine series, configured with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates a 260 MB Level 3 cache along with advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES and VAES.

The instance is provisioned with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding exactly 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file systems and OS operations. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional processing throughput under parallelized workloads, highlighted by top-tier image processing and strong Geekbench multi-core performance exceeding 20,000 points. PassMark testing confirms strong extended instruction and cryptographic execution, bolstered by AMX and AVX-512 extensions.

Memory subsystem benchmarks reveal strong uncached throughput, sustaining 249.73 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 102.08 GB/sec in write tests, though smaller cached operations score in the average tier. Real-world workload evaluations demonstrate high throughput across network and processing services, reaching 64.82 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 78.25 GB/sec on static web serving benchmarks. LLM inference testing shows strong performance during prompt processing and token generation on small and medium parameter models.

By omitting bundled local NVMe storage and limiting the system memory allocation to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D48ls_v6 offers a resource-efficient footprint for CPU-bound infrastructure where dense RAM is unnecessary. The instance is suited for batch processing, software compilation pipelines, web application fleets, microservice hosting, and distributed database nodes that scale compute independently from persistent storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 260 MB L3 cache, the system incorporates advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance does not feature local storage or discrete GPUs, operating via remote Azure Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core processing, fast clang compilation, and robust memory bandwidth on large blocks, alongside sustained Redis throughput reaching 64.82 million operations per second. Its lean memory profile delivers efficient compute allocation for CPU-intensive workloads such as continuous integration build agents, web clusters, media processing, and distributed network services.
